question: How much will Nvidia's stock price returns exceed Apple's in these biweekly periods of Q4 2026? (Nov 23 - Dec 4)

calls.reasoning: Reference class: NVDA-AAPL fortnightly return spreads, normally SD ~6-7pp centered near zero. Current regime is extreme: Jensen Huang ousted ~Nov 12, NVDA -16% this week (-7% on Nov 20, ~$136), 7-day losing streak, Nasdaq -3.6% on the day, while AAPL is stable near $349. Catalysts in window: possible permanent CEO naming (upside), Huang/GC congressional interviews Dec 1-2 and the export-control probe (downside), plus oversold-bounce potential. Median slightly positive for short-term reversal, with wide fat tails and ~9% total mass outside +/-15. No human market prices this spread; Kalshi/Polymarket only list CEO-related contracts.
calls.reference_class: Biweekly NVDA minus AAPL percent-return spreads 2023-2026, scaled up for the current crisis-volatility regime

calls.reasoning: Window Nov 23-Dec 4 (P0 = Nov 20 close, 9 trading days). NVDA is in a high-vol regime: -7.5% on Nov 20, 7-day losing streak, -24% MTD after CEO Huang's Nov 12 resignation and an AI/chip selloff, VIX ~31, 30d IV ~52% with an options-implied +/-5.3% move to Nov 27. AAPL is calm near its ATH (~$350) and acting as a safe haven. Spread SD comes out ~8-10pp, wider than the normal ~5-7pp for biweekly NVDA-AAPL gaps. Median is slightly positive (+0.5) for an oversold-bounce tendency (RSI ~18), offset by scandal/AI-capex momentum. Tails beyond +/-15pp are priced at ~4% each side. No matching human market found; Polymarket's largest-company market (Apple ~83-89%) is a different contract, treated only as sentiment evidence.
